analysis.title: Rates Spark: Inflation pricing sends mixed signals
key_insights: Markets price near-term inflation risk (reinforced by this week's US CPI surprise and still-high energy prices) but long-term inflation expectations remain low by historical standards. ING sees the structural inflation risk as possibly underpriced.
The 5Y5Y EUR inflation swap is 2.07%, only slightly above the ECB's 2% target. Before the global financial crisis it was often near 2.4%. The gap to pre-GFC levels is larger for the US.
ING argues the post-2008 period of low inflation swap rates, when inflation failed to return to 2%, was exceptional and should not be treated as the norm.
Growth is healthy, central banks have room to ease, and low unemployment means wages can quickly add to price pressures. Global tensions raise the risk of supply shocks.

High government debt is hard to sustain if policy rates stay high, which can raise financial stability concerns. ING says central banks may be forced to tolerate higher inflation and may lean dovish rather than risk a sovereign debt crisis.
ING draws a parallel between the volatility around France and a possible US fiscal test. Its baseline has favourable inflation dynamics, but it sees risks tilted to the upside.
Thursday calendar: UK GDP, US weekly jobless claims, October US federal budget balance, and central bank speakers (ECB's Nagel and Lagarde, Fed's Schmid and Williams).
Thursday supply: UK £4bn 6y Gilts, Italy €7.25bn total across 3y BTPs, 7y BTPs and 20y Green BTPs, and US $25bn new 30y Bonds.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets price long-term inflation near target (5Y5Y EUR swap at 2.07%). Growth is healthy and central banks have room to ease, so inflation stays benign.
tension_points.bear_case: Fiscal pressure may force central banks to tolerate higher inflation, and supply shocks and tight labour markets can add to prices. Pre-GFC pricing was near 2.4%.
